sources.title: Use MergeKit to Extract LoRA Adapters from any Fine-Tuned Model
sources.snippet: Exciting news from Arcee! You can now extract LoRA adapters from any fine-tuned model using MergeKit. Example: The fine-tuned model is compared against a base model, and the differences in parameter values (sometimes called task vector) are decomposed into a PEFT-compatible low-rank adapter that approximates the task vector.

sources.title: LoRA Extraction | arcee-ai/mergekit | DeepWiki
sources.snippet: This page documents the mergekit-extract-lora command, which extracts a PEFT-compatible LoRA adapter from the difference between a fine-tuned model and its base model using truncated singular value decomposition (SVD). This tool produces adapters that are directly loadable by the PEFT library.

sources.title: I made a thing : extract a LoRA adapter from any model
sources.snippet: The thing is, because the Lora was trained on top of finetuned model (not a base model), you can extract it, but this lora works basically "more or less" only on the same finetuned model - as the previous finetuning changed all the weights of the base.
